title: Colombo National Museum panels: Transitional Period / Political History / Economy & Society / Religion & Culture
author_or_institution: Colombo National Museum / Department of National Museums, Sri Lanka
author_institution: Department of National Museums, Sri Lanka
scope: Museum synthesis of Dambadeniya, Yapahuwa, Kurunegala, Gampola, Kotte and Sitawaka; trade, religion and foreign intervention
limitations: Modern institutional synthesis. Dates, causal language, normative claims about the Sangha, and named diplomatic/military episodes require independent scholarly or primary corroboration.

title: The political history of the Kingdoms of Yapahuwa, Kurunegala and Gampala
date: publication date unresolved; repository metadata accessed 2026-09-01
scope: Political fragmentation, Yapahuwa destruction, Kurunegala and Gampola transitions
limitations: Repository thesis/monograph record; use alongside epigraphic/chronicle evidence for episode-level precision. Exact publication metadata remains to be recovered.

title: Yapahuwa Rock Fortress
scope: Yapahuwa fortification, Tooth Relic and Pandyan seizure
limitations: Public heritage synthesis; military chronology should be cross-checked against specialist history.

title: The Long 13th Century of Tambralinga
author_or_institution: Yoneo Ishii / Memoirs of the Research Department of the Toyo Bunko
scope: Chandrabhanu/Tambralinga and invasions of Sri Lanka in the thirteenth century
limitations: Chronology follows a specific scholarly reconstruction; retain uncertainty where source traditions differ.

title: Mamluk record tradition for Bhuvanekabahu I embassy to Egypt, 1283
author_or_institution: Sabaragamuwa University journal article drawing on al-Maqrizi/Quatremere
scope: 1283 embassy, Sultan Qalawun, Muslim envoy al-Hajj Abu Uthman and trade/diplomatic context
limitations: The medieval Arabic text is mediated through later editions/translations; recover a critical edition before verbatim quotation in final narrative.

title: The Kingdom of Jaffna
scope: Aryacakravarti formation, Pandyan/Vijayanagara relations, Kotte conquest and Jaffna political history
limitations: Some early chronology remains historiographically debated; distinguish direct epigraphic evidence from later narrative sources.

title: The Jaffna (Main Street) Inscription of the reign of Parakramabahu VI
scope: Inscriptional evidence for Parakramabahu VI authority in Jaffna
limitations: Use the published inscription/transcription itself for exact wording; current URL is a later monograph reproducing/discussing it, so the T0 label applies to the underlying published inscription rather than to the convenience URL.

title: The Munnesvaram Tamil Inscription of Parakramabahu VI
author_or_institution: S. Pathmanathan / Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society (Sri Lanka)
scope: Parakramabahu VI, conquest of Jaffna, South Indian influence and mercantile/Brahmanical networks
limitations: Conquest detail combines inscriptional evidence with literary sources; keep layers distinct.

title: Ming–Kotte War in Southeast Asia (1410–11)
scope: Zheng He/Ming intervention and capture of Kotte ruler/Alakeshvara in 1410–1411
limitations: Specific identification/titling of the captured ruler varies across source traditions; chronology may be rendered 1410/1411.

title: Circles of kings and right of the port: maritime violence and the galactic polity in 14th-century Sri Lanka
scope: Kotte/Raigama, port taxation, Colombo/Beruwala, maritime violence and political authority
limitations: Focuses primarily on fourteenth-century political economy; do not project unchanged mechanisms across the whole transitional period.

title: From village to state, and back again: cycles of de-urbanization and adaptation in Early Historic and Medieval Sri Lanka
scope: Post-Polonnaruwa capitals, de-urbanisation/adaptation and repeated relocation of political centres
limitations: Archaeological interpretation remains a developing research area; avoid treating all later capitals as identical functional forms.
